thread:
Sophia: heads up — after the kube rollout we pushed last night we're seeing ~18% regression at P99 for short-turn requests. traces point at host-side tokenize + grpc writev overhead.

Mike: link to the trace? small sample pls

Sophia: https://perf.internal/runs/2026-03-17/mini-stream-heap — top hotspots from flamegraph:
- host.tokenize() ~37%
- grpc.writev (many tiny syscalls) ~22%
- parser.readFrames / framing ~15%

Priya: hmm. that pattern screams fragmentation of streaming chunks + tiny batches. kernel choice itself is OK — it's the request shaping on the host before it hits the runtime.

Dan: ran a microbench this morning. baseline (current) vs batching-hint experiment:
```
bench: 10k short requests (mean 12 tokens)
baseline p50 28ms p99 210ms
hinting p50 25ms p99 190ms
syscalls/writev count per request: baseline 6 -> hinting 2
```

Sophia: nice. experiment details? how did you supply the hint?

Dan: added a tiny proto field on the ingress envelope: tokenizer_hint_tokens (uint32). the tokenizer on host sets it after a fast pre-tokenize pass. runtime uses it to pick batch window + kernel length class.

Mike: curious about semantics — is that leaking token counts? privacy concern?

Sophia: it's only an approximate integer (rounded to nearest 8), capped at 256, and option to disable per-customer. no text or tokenizer output gets sent. it's similar to existing size hints we have for embeddings.

Priya: can you paste the proto snippet? thinking about compatibility.

Dan: sure
```
message IngressEnvelope {
  // existing fields...
  optional uint32 tokenizer_hint_tokens = 3103; // approximate token count, rounded
}
```

Sophia: implementation notes — we do a cheap char-based pre-scan that estimates token count; cost ~0.6us per request and avoids a full unicode/tokenizer allocation path in the hot path.

Mike: and how does runtime consume it? kernel selector?

Priya: yes — kernel selector now maps hint -> kernel class (short/medium/long) and chooses batching window. we added a small hysteresis counter to avoid flip-flopping for requests that oscillate near a boundary.

Sophia: results from the canary run (24h, mixed traffic) — overall p50 improved 6%, p99 improved 7-12% depending on region. writev syscalls down ~2.8x for short-turns. KV cache miss rate dropped slightly because prefix boundaries are more consistent.

Mike: KV behavior improvement is interesting — how does hinting affect prefix matching?

Priya: when streaming chunk boundaries align differently we used to produce different prefix splits which fragmented the KV cache. hinting lets the ingress produce chunking that matches runtime's expected prefix lengths so KV keys align more often.

Sophia: also found a small regression case: for extremely long single-shot prompts (>> hint cap) the heuristic favored a short-kernel class if hint was zero (opt-out), which caused extra kernel swaps. PR fixes: default to medium for unknown.

Dan: opened PR: https://git.internal/rw/ingress/+/3456 — includes unit tests, opt-out flag, and docs. also added metric: ingress.tokenize_fragment_size.histogram

infra-bot: canary deploy started for svc-host-parse pool=mini-token rev=rev-2026-03-17-3

Mike: action items:
1) add tokenizer_hint_tokens to public proto changelog (compat note)
2) ship canary for 72h and collect p50/p95/p99, writev syscall counts, kv-prefix-alignment%
3) run stress tests for long prompts (cover fallback path)
4) add test that ensures opt-out customers see no hint field

Sophia: I'll take 1+4, assigning this thread and will open a follow-up doc describing the pre-scan algorithm. @Mike you monitor canary dashboards? :thumbsup:

Mike: yup. I'll watch and post updates in #eng-runtime-canary. if p99 stays within 3% of baseline after 72h we can promote.

Priya: one more note — if we roll this out widely we should consider exposing a coarse 'batching_priority' enum instead of exact counts for even less leakage.

Sophia: agreed. short-term: tokenizer_hint_tokens remains internal-only. long-term API discussion separate.

Mike: thanks all — good win for host-side overhead. small change but big payback on writev/sock churn and KV alignment.

Sophia: posting perf artifacts to the run; will link RFC once PR is green.

Dan: :rocket:

infra-bot: canary metrics: looped p99 delta +8% -> +2% over 14h (stabilizing)

Mike: keep this thread pinned for follow-ups. closing after 72h unless any bumps.
